outcome: Perioperative complications (operating room time, length of hospital stay, surgical complications)
cohort: 18,184 patients in British Columbia, Canada, who underwent either opportunistic salpingectomy or tubal ligation during Cesarean section
finding: Opportunistic salpingectomy at the time of Cesarean section was associated with decreased perioperative complications and no difference in postoperative complications compared to tubal ligation, but an increased likelihood of filling prescriptions for nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs and opioids postoperatively.
mod_finding: This study found that opportunistic salpingectomy (OS) performed during a cesarean section was associated with decreased perioperative complications compared to tubal ligation, with no difference in postoperative complications.
